title: Hybrid tenant pin orchestration decision note
summary: Working note describing an orchestration pattern for hybrid tenant pinning: tenant-owned region preferences + platform-enforced pin semantics with graceful fallback to hosted variants. Focus is operator flows, telemetry needed to prove evidence, and a staged migration path for enterprise customers.
scope: Define a minimal orchestration layer and operator playbook to support customers who require a mixed model: core inference in customer-owned region (pin) while allowing non-sensitive auxiliary workloads to run in Redwood-hosted regions. Does NOT cover full billing model or per-token encryption knobs — those are separate follow-ups.
assumptions: Tenants can supply a region pin (cloud region code or VPC identifier) at onboarding
We have capacity reservation APIs for Dedicated/Private to pin GPU pools
Customers accept a documented fallback behavior for transient outages
Platform can emit per-request pin evidence (region, host id, timestamp) into audit logs
proposal_high_level: Introduce a lightweight orchestrator that records per-tenant pin intent and provides a deterministic routing decision. Orchestrator stores: tenant_pin (region or 'on-prem'), pin_mode (strict | preferred | staged), pin_ttl, last_verified. Router consults orchestrator then routing table. For strict mode, requests that cannot be served in-region are rejected with a documented error code and audit event.
operator_flows: Onboarding: Solutions engineer records tenant_pin and selects pin_mode. Orchestrator creates reservation ticket and checks capacity. If capacity shortfall, raise sales support alert.

Normal ops: Router consults orchestrator in read-only fast path (cached for 30s). If in-region capacity exists, route. If not, apply pin_mode policy (fail or fallback). Emit events: PIN_ROUTE_{OK, FALLBACK, FAIL}.
Pin verification: daily background job verifies that tenant pinned region still has active reservation. If mismatch set last_verified stale and alert owner channel.
Emergency failover: During prolonged outage, operator can set tenant pin_mode=preferred to allow fallback; change must be recorded and customer notified via email template.
telemetry_requirements: Per-request tagged fields: tenant_id, tenant_pin, routed_region, host_id, decision_source (orchestrator|local-cache), outcome (served|fallback|rejected)
Pin evidence bundle available in audit logs for 90 days: request_id, route_decision, proof_host_fingerprint, timestamp
Alerting: percent of tenant traffic hitting fallback > 1% over 5m should page on-call for pin capacity
Cost telemetry: estimate delta tokens cost when fallback used vs in-region serving (daily aggregate per tenant)
migration_path_for_existing_customers: Phase 0 (inventory): run a data residency scan to classify tenants by country/legal regime. Produce CSV: tenant_id, recommended_pin, sensitivity_flag.
Phase 1 (opt-in): contact high-sensitivity customers and propose pin_mode default=preferred to test routing; capture acceptance as agreement ticket.
Phase 2 (enforcement pilot): pick 3 customers for strict pin pilot. Stand up reservation and run 72h controlled traffic tests. Collect telemetry and regression evals.
Phase 3 (rollout): gradual roll to strict mode by tier (enterprise -> mid-market -> small), with fallback windows and eskalation playbooks
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator API completed with CRUD for tenant pin and pin_mode
Router consults orchestrator with cache misses < 10ms median impact on tail latency
Telemetry exposes PIN_ROUTE_{OK,FALLBACK,FAIL} events in prod and they correlate with host-level evidence
Pilot customers report no unexplained region routing errors over 2 weeks
slo_and_sla_notes: For pinned tenants in strict mode: 99.9% successful in-region routing over 30d. Fallback events must include automated customer-facing explanation and remediation steps. SLA exceptions during planned maintenance must be pre-notified and recorded.
cost_modeling_notes: Quick model: fallback to hosted region increases infra delta by ~10–35% depending on batching and KV cache locality. We need a meter labeled 'pin_fallback_tokens' to credibly bill/credit customers or reconcile cost.
security_and_compliance_considerations: KMS integration: when tenant_pin=on-prem or VPC, ensure keys used for request-level HMAC are tenant-scoped
Audit chain: signed evidence for routing decision (orchestrator signature + host fingerprint) to satisfy legal eDiscovery
Data retention: logs containing pin evidence must be retained with same retention as other audit logs and support export on legal request
open_questions: What is the canonical identifier for a 'region pin' — cloud region code OR customer VPC id? (impacts routing table granularity)
How do we handle multi-region tenants that require active-active (split pins)?
Who owns billing adjustments when fallback occurs? platform or customer? need finance input
What UI in Console to expose pin state and historical evidence to customers?
